sentence_stem: Had the company invested in staff training,
correct_completion: it would not have lost so many customers.
full_sentence: Had the company invested in staff training, it would not have lost so many customers.
acceptable_variants: it wouldn't have lost so many customers.
it would have kept far more of its customers.

options.text: it will not lose many customers today.
options.why_wrong: An inverted third conditional needs a 'would have' result clause to describe an imagined past outcome; 'will not lose ... today' refers to the present or future instead.

options.text: the company loses customers every year.
options.why_wrong: This states a general fact and does not complete the hypothetical result of the condition introduced by 'had'.

options.text: it would not have lost so many customers.
it has lost so many customers recently.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect reports a real past fact, not the imagined result of an unreal condition.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (Had + subject + past participle, without 'if')
explanation: Here 'had' begins an inverted conditional clause that replaces 'if', so the main clause must use 'would have' plus a past participle. Portuguese speakers often try to use a simple past or a plain future in the result clause, because Portuguese conditional structures are built differently; in English the result must match the unreal past condition.
translation: Se a empresa tivesse investido em treinamento da equipe, não teria perdido tantos clientes.
